concept.title: How Content Fusion Finds DITA References
concept.shortdesc: The References tab in the Explore side view shows how files in a DITA project reference one another. Use it to identify what a change affects before you make it and to understand how a large project fits together.

conbody.note: The References tab is experimental. To enable it, open your Profile page and select Show the DITA References tab in the Explore side view in the Preferences section. This setting applies only to the current browser. The tab is available for projects that define publications.

section.title: Where the References Come From
section.p: The References tab reads the workspace files in the browser. It starts with the root map of each publication and follows every reference it finds, reaching every file used by a publication. A file that no publication reaches has no references in the tab.
The tab identifies the following types of references:

strow.stentry: topicref, mapref, keydef, key definitions, aliases made with copy-to, reltable, ditavalref, subject scheme references, and the publications of the project file
conref, conkeyref, conref push, coderef, and include
image, media, object, and other references to files that are not DITA

p.note: DITA specializations that use different element names are not currently supported.

section.p: The tab calls a non-DITA file, such as an image, a resource. Most references lead to a file, but some lead to a key, an alias, or a web address. See .

section.title: Incoming references
section.p: You can determine the files that a file references by inspecting that file. The References tab also shows where a file is referenced on the Referenced by tab. After the tab loads, you can instantly navigate to the incoming references of any file.

section.title: Project Scope and Publication Scope
section.p: By default, the References tab covers the whole project (every file that any publication uses). In this project scope:

ul.li: The tab applies no profiling, so it shows every reference, even if it is excluded from all publications.
The tab does not resolve keys by key scope. All keys with the same name are treated as one key, even when they belong to different key scopes.

section.p: The Use the context publication as scope toolbar button limits the tab to the context publication. In this publication scope, the tab processes maps as the publication does: it applies DITAVAL profiling, resolves keys within their key scopes, and follows copy-to. A file excluded by the publication has no references in this scope.
Use the project scope to find everything a change can affect across all publications. Use the publication scope to see what a context publication includes or why a key resolves as it does.

section.title: When the Tab Reads the Files
section.p: The tab reads the files when it opens and retains what it finds. It does not update when you edit, save, or commit files. After changing files, click Refresh to read them again.
Reading a large project can take time, and the tab shows its progress. While it reads, additional references to the selected file can appear in the Referenced by list.

ul.li: The tab treats XML files that are not DITA, and files in formats that it does not know, as resources. It does not look for references inside them.
In the publication scope, the tab does not apply chunking and ignores the linking attribute.
Large projects take longer to read.
